content.definition: True or false by the meanings of its words alone, like 'All bachelors are unmarried'.
True or false depending on how the world is, like 'Some swans are black'.

content.text: A priori knowledge comes from reason alone. A posteriori knowledge needs experience. The first pair is about what makes a statement true. The second is about how we know it.

examples.title: Analytic
lines: Nothing is red all over and green all over at once.
examples.note: No observation is needed. Denying these contradicts what the words mean.

examples.title: Synthetic
lines: Water boils at 100 °C under standard air pressure.
examples.note: You have to look at the world to know these.

options: The sun rises in the east
question.hint: Which one can you know from the meanings of its words alone?
question.explanation: Being female is part of what 'sister' means, so 'All sisters are female' is analytic. The others need observation.
